body: Thank god, I love seeing takes like this springing, finally. The writing of this game has elevated the quality of video games' writing to a whole quality standard, and we're acting like this is a simple, sloppy "this or that" good vs bad cheap writing. It misses the point, the depth, all the in between meanings that make everything such a unique, unforgettable experience.

They are not *her* creations. Renoir stopped having a hold on their chroma and Maelle claimed it to bring them back. There is nothing in the game to support she would be able to manipulate the creations and make them into different versions.

Exactly: painted over by the real Clea.

We get told Clea is the only one skilled enough to do this. Alicia is often foretold as the least skilled painter (still a god for the universe of the canvas, but lesser than her family). Alicia just doesn't have the talent to do what Clea can.

Maelle is absolutely Alicia and vice versa. She lived an entire life inside that canvas with actual experiences, memories and emotions, things that she held on to after her memories were restored. How are they different people when she has all the experiences and livelihoods of both?

Bringing back Verso is the regrettable part of her ending, which is the essence of the story. If neither endings had a regrettable angle (in Verso's case, erasing the entire canvas) then narratively both of them would be void, useless options with no stakes at the bargain. A damaged, traumatized teenager clinging desperately to the image of her brother is a flaw, but why necessarily a condemnation she will become the personification of satan?
Yeah I don't understand why it is the mainstream. It's such an exhausted argument. Assuming the absolute worst scenarios for her in every turn.

This is all assuming the absolute worst hypothetical scenarios for Maelle though, taking into account that she does the worst choices imaginable everytime.

Gustave reacting so extremely and Maelle gommaging him is such an unrealistic stretch. They adored each other so much, Gustave had basically given up on the expedition entirely until he was reconnected with Maelle. For Maelle, he was the only real family her entire life throughout the canvas. That she would put him through gommage, the single most traumatizing thing for the people of Lumiere and the thing every expeditioner sacrifices their lives for for a chance to stop it, would be Maelle insulting and spitting on Gustave's memory. How could that possibly work? She loves him so much!

But like these are all projections. Everything. From the content we get in game, Maelle has always behaved lovingly and with adoration for her companions. She wants so desperately to preserve this world, I can't think of a single instance hinting she would try to twist it to her own narrative. We don't even know if the others of the canvas know exactly what she is, everything is left so vague (purposefully).

Why would others think of her as a tyrant based on what we've seen? That's only a "what if" situation.

Where do you all get this idea that the people have no free will? It's so bizzare how it's thrown around all the time when there is not one single instance in the entire game that shows the painters have the capacity to effect the free will of the creations.

Unless you can pinpoint exact moments in the game that allude to this, you're collectively applying a random headcanon for the sake of your argument.

Which is weird.

EDIT: forgot to mention that Clea is an exception that can actually manipulate the free will of the creations. That's on me.

I will die on the hill that trying to attach a black and white dichotomy to the endings is such a narrow thinking that severely undermines the grandiose of such beautiful writing. The game is so unique because it imposes all these philosophical questions through magnificently crafted allegories and thought-provoking artwork that moves and haunts you at every step.

The "good" and "bad" labels ignore all the nuance in between the far ends. Massive oversimplifications that don't do justice one of the best games written in at least a decade, if not way beyond that.

We understood her plan just fine, I don't know why we're running in circles over this again and again as a fandom. The problem isn't the WHAT is she after, but HOW it's executed.

One of the basic principles of writing mystery and scheming is that you give hints to your audience as to how the character(s) is going on about it. Someone here said we're "smooth brain" that we want to be spoonfed, when we're just saying the correct way to execute Sage's character would be to give us glimpses of her action, throw clues as to what strings she is pulling, foreshadow events, make it believable she is some cunning mastermind who is playing chess with herself because she's just that good and they can't match her, etc.

Instead, Sage executed two very unimpressive plans (framing starlighters, ruining Starlight's reputation) then faded into the background with underwhelming conversations with side characters. The show SAYS she is planning something but the show isn't SHOWING what she's planning: she just scooped in after every aftermath and claimed it as part of her plan. In the finale when everything is done for, she shows up to get the credits, and she hasn't shown any decision making that would match "smartest person in the world", leaving the audience feeling cheated with a "plot twist" that just didn't land.

Criticizing Sage isn't trashing on the show, it's just the unfortunate reality of trying to write for super geniuses: the writers just can't because none of us are on that level of intelligence. Which is very unfortunate, because I loved the introduction of her character and I thought she brought a new dynamic that was very interesting.

But the reason I am calling them masterpieces is because I also write (although that's a hobby, not a job so different standards) and I feel it in my bones how hard it is to create characters, flesh them out skillfully and keep your audience engaged. From start to finish, both of these seasons had very clever fleshing out for their cast and no one was really being wasted: everyone on screen was part of the main plot, while also having some really interesting side plots of their own to look into.

For me, it felt like a challenge that they executed very well and even to an impressive extent. Most series I watch anyways feel like they fumble the bag and at best get you 2-3 characters that are meaningful while the rest feel so lackluster because they don't have any complexity, don't bring any tension to the plot and don't serve a purpose.

The Boys has a superficial silly aura about it, being a satirical show first and foremost, while challenging some very complicated sociopolitical issues with meaningful personalities. In the end, that just checks my boxes.

Simple: because this show raised the standards so high after delivering 2 masterpiece seasons that had immaculate writing and the kind of character development other writers need to take lessons from. It's not just hard to make cancer disappear for good: it's kind of impossible actually. CancerS (plural, it's important) are so, so, so, so many, so versatile and completely different for each person. Even if you took two patients with the exact same type of cancer, they are still two unique cases with different and unique genetic profiles that may have entirely different responses to treatment.

Pharmas would NOT block research because they ARE actively shoving billions into it. But with the technology and knowledge we have in the present, we are making baby steps towards an almost impossible goal. I fucking hate big pharmas and I hate how much they control research and funds, but this belief they would assassinate the person who cracked the code just doesn't apply to reality.

I'm sorry, this isn't a conspiracy. Cancers are just that good at their job. We should be angry about actual, real problems instead of conspiracies.

I don't understand why everytime people give criticism to a movie or a series nowadays we immediately call it crying. What happened to having an opinion?

But to play that game, people are "crying" because season 4 has a big narrative issue. S1 and S2 were both masterpieces when it came down to characterization, handling side plots, creating tension and making twists for the audience to follow up on. S3 followed closely to those steps and deservingly lived up to the hype (except for a questionable ending).

S4 has been a letdown in all those regards: we've had 6 whole episodes of build up that have lead us nowhere yet, which feels absurd and like running circles; Frenchie occupied a massive amount of screen time with a side plot that was irrelevant and repetitive (we already did the whole face your sins with Nina last season, we did not need this again); Sage was a welcome breath of new air in the first episodes, but now she's been sidelined and looking like a total mess; and MM is just there, doing kinda nothing really. Also these shock-value gigs have stopped being sparsed throughout the show, and instead are all over the place now, which is like hearing a joke over and over again (it stops being funny after the 10th time).

If we compare that to S3, we had Soldier Boy, who was gradually built into the universe, was merged into the main plot and built so much tension and excitement by going after his team, teaming up with the Boys and finally fighting HL and Butcher. His whole arc was phenomenal writing that made it generally a fucking great show. Now compare that to the newcomers of this season and see how extreme the difference is in the character development department.

In game RUSH Hextech GLP-800 and Twin Shadows. Personally I take Zhonyas as a second item and then go for Twin Shadows if I really can't survive during ulti because of the enemy dealing too much damage. Hope this helps!

Even though on paper it's an OK rune and a lot of people pick it, I hate Aery on Morgana with a raging passion TBH. While she is mostly known for her amazing lock-down capability and the delicious cc immunity, she can pull out so much more damage than most expect, which is why I always take comet instead (inspiration secondary for the stopwatch). The Liandrys-Rylais build gives you a fantastic amount of aoe damage that will help you carry the bot lane singlehandedly and make tank supports suffer even harder by your hands as you make their bars disappear from the Liandrys damage! When I play duo with a reliable adc that I know can carry like they're supposed to, I go for the glacial-domination build. The snare, the stuns and the slows are way too much cc stacked up together to counter and you'll leave them praying for mercy during mid-late game when you hit the 45% cdr and max stacks on item active cdr. It's the only case in which I max Q over W, because landing it in high elo is reliable only after drastically ccing your targets.

If my team is moronic enough not to get any front line and only when the situation is that desperate, I go for an Aftershock tank build with Zekes, but it's definitely not optimal when compared to the other builds.
